web.isolation.title: How artifacts are kept apart
web.isolation.single.title: Single domain
web.isolation.single.body: Artifacts are served from this same address, under /c/. Every response tells the browser to run the page in a sealed sandbox, so it cannot read or set Pinwall's cookies or act as you. It still shares this domain with anything else hosted on it, which makes it weaker than a separate domain. Needs nothing extra.
web.isolation.content.title: Separate content domain
web.isolation.content.body: Each version is served from its own address on a domain used for nothing else, such as <token>.pinwall-content.example. Browsers keep it fully apart from Pinwall and from other versions. Needs a second domain with a wildcard DNS record and certificate. Recommended for production.
web.isolation.tradeoff: Both modes keep artifacts away from your Pinwall session. Single domain is the easiest to run; a separate content domain isolates best. Links people hold keep working when you switch; switching means setting PINWALL_ISOLATION (and PINWALL_CONTENT_ORIGIN) and restarting Pinwall.

web.config.title: Configuration
web.config.envNote: These settings come from environment variables. Pinwall shows them but never changes them: edit your deployment and restart.
web.config.help.PINWALL_PUBLIC_ORIGIN: The address people use to open Pinwall; every link, cookie and redirect is built from it.
web.config.help.PINWALL_HOST: The network address Pinwall listens on; 0.0.0.0 means every network interface.
web.config.help.PINWALL_DATA_DIR: The folder that holds the SQLite database, locally stored files and the generated secret key.
web.config.help.PINWALL_SECRET_KEY: The key that Pinwall's encryption and signing keys come from; it always shows as set, because Pinwall generates it into the data folder when you do not give one.
web.config.help.PINWALL_TRUST_PROXY: Which reverse proxies Pinwall believes when they say who is visiting: false trusts none, true trusts one proxy in front, and a list names trusted proxy networks.
web.config.help.PINWALL_METRICS_PORT: The port of the separate listener that serves /metrics; 0 turns it off.
web.config.help.PINWALL_LOG_LEVEL: How much the server writes to its log, from fatal (least) to trace (most).
web.config.help.PINWALL_WEB_DIR: The folder the web app is served from; not set means the copy bundled with Pinwall.
web.config.help.PINWALL_ISOLATION: Where artifact pages are served from, single-domain or content-domain; both are explained above, and changing it takes a restart.
web.config.help.PINWALL_CONTENT_ORIGIN: The separate domain artifacts are served from in content-domain mode, such as https://pinwall-content.example; it must not be Pinwall's own address or a parent of it.
web.config.help.PINWALL_DATABASE_URL: Where Pinwall keeps its data, a SQLite file or a PostgreSQL address; passwords are never shown here.
web.config.help.PINWALL_DATABASE_POOL_SI: How many PostgreSQL connections Pinwall keeps open; it only applies to PostgreSQL.
web.config.help.PINWALL_STORAGE: Where artifact files are stored: local (in the data folder) or s3 (an S3-compatible bucket).
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_BUCKET: The bucket that holds artifact files.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_REGION: The region the bucket lives in.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_ENDPOINT: The address of an S3-compatible service such as MinIO; not set means Amazon S3.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: The access key id Pinwall signs in to the bucket with; hidden, and when no key pair is set Pinwall uses the credentials of the machine it runs on.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_SECRET_ACCESS: The secret that goes with the access key id; hidden.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_FORCE_PATH_ST: Whether requests put the bucket name in the path instead of the host name, which many S3-compatible services need.
web.config.help.PINWALL_S3_PREFIX: A prefix added in front of every file Pinwall stores, so one bucket can be shared.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_ISSUER: The address of your identity provider; single sign-on is on only when this and the client id are set.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_CLIENT_ID: The client id Pinwall is registered under at your identity provider.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_CLIENT_SECR: The client secret that goes with the client id; hidden.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_SCOPES: What Pinwall asks your identity provider to share about someone who signs in; it must include openid.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_DISPLAY_NAM: The name on the single sign-on button.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_EXTRA_AUTH_: Extra settings sent with the sign-in request, written as key=value pairs joined by &.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_ALLOW_HTTP_: Whether an identity provider reached over plain http is allowed; leave it false unless that provider is on a private network, because http traffic can be read and changed on the way.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_ROLES_CLAIM: The field in the sign-in token that lists a person's groups or roles.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_ADMIN_GROUP: People in any of these identity provider groups become admins.
web.config.help.PINWALL_OIDC_MEMBER_GROU: People in any of these identity provider groups become members.
web.config.help.PINWALL_ADMIN_EMAILS: People who sign in with a verified email on this list become admins.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MEMBER_EMAILS: People who sign in with a verified email on this list become members.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MEMBER_DOMAINS: People whose verified email is in one of these domains become members; when no member group, email or domain is set, everyone the identity provider admits is a member.
web.config.help.PINWALL_ACCESS_RECHECK_I: How often Pinwall asks your identity provider whether a person still has access.
web.config.help.PINWALL_VISIBILITY: team: every member sees every project, as in Pinwall 1.0. personal: each person sees only the projects they own or were added to. Takes a restart.
web.config.help.PINWALL_SHARE_LINKS: members: anyone may share, as in Pinwall 1.0. approved: only admins and the people you approve in Users may make share links and raw links.
web.config.help.PINWALL_ABUSE_CONTACT: An email address or an http(s) URL where people report abuse; shown on share pages, on the pages for links that are gone or not found, and on the sign-in page.
web.config.help.PINWALL_TERMS_URL: An http(s) URL of your terms of use, linked from the sign-in page.
web.config.help.PINWALL_PRIVACY_URL: An http(s) URL of your privacy notice, linked from the sign-in page.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES: The largest single upload request Pinwall accepts.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_INLINE_BYTES: The most content an agent can send inline in one publish over MCP.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_FILE_BYTES: The largest single file inside an artifact version.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_VERSION_BYTE: The largest total size of an artifact version once it is unpacked.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_FILES: The most files one artifact version can hold.
web.config.help.PINWALL_MAX_EXPANSION_RA: How many times larger than its zip file an upload may unpack to, which stops zip bombs.
web.config.help.PINWALL_QUOTA_BYTES: The most each person may store, as the total size of their versions; 0 means no limit, admins have none, and you can set another value for one person.
web.config.help.PINWALL_QUOTA_ARTIFACTS: The most artifacts each person may have; 0 means no limit, admins have none, and you can set another value for one person.
web.config.help.PINWALL_SESSION_TTL: How long a browser stays signed in without being used; each visit extends it.
web.config.help.PINWALL_PREVIEW_TTL: How long the access Pinwall grants for viewing an artifact lasts, in the review viewer and in raw links.
web.config.help.PINWALL_UPLOAD_SESSION_T: How long a started upload may take to finish before Pinwall discards it.

publish.path.link: {{path}} is a symbolic or hard link, and links are not allowed. Archive the file itself (tar -h follows symlinks).
publish.path.special: {{path}} is a device, FIFO or other special file. Only regular files and folders are allowed.

publish.limit.max_version_bytes: The files add up to more than {{max}} bytes (PINWALL_MAX_VERSION_BYTES).
publish.limit.max_files: The upload has more than {{max}} files (PINWALL_MAX_FILES).
publish.limit.max_expansion_ratio: The archive expands to more than {{max}} times its compressed size (PINWALL_MAX_EXPANSION_RATIO), so it looks like an archive bomb.
publish.limit.max_inline_bytes: The inline files add up to more than {{max}} bytes (PINWALL_MAX_INLINE_BYTES). Use an upload URL instead.
publish.archive.corrupt: The archive is damaged or truncated and could not be read.
publish.archive.zip64: ZIP64 archives are not supported. Send a tar.gz instead: tar -czf - -C <folder> .
publish.archive.zipMethod: {{path}} uses a ZIP compression method other than store or deflate.
publish.archive.encrypted: {{path}} is encrypted, and encrypted archives are not supported.
publish.warning.rootAbsolute: {{file}} refers to {{url}} from the server root, which does not load in single-domain mode. Use a relative path.
publish.versionConflict: The artifact has a newer version (v{{number}}) than the one this publish replaces. Fetch the artifact again and publish on top of v{{number}}.
publish.unsupported: Send a tar, tar.gz or zip archive, or a single file with Content-Type text/html or text/markdown, or add ?filename=<name> to the URL.
publish.inline.interrupted: The request was interrupted before all of it arrived. Send it again.
publish.inline.textOnly: {{path}}: inline publish takes text files only (HTML, Markdown, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, JSON). Use an upload URL for other files.
publish.path.encoding: {{path}}: the name is not valid Unicode text (it contains a lone surrogate).

publish.session.expired: This upload URL has expired. Ask for a new one with the create_publish_session tool or POST /api/v1/publish-sessions.

publish.upload.form: Send multipart/form-data with a target field and at least one file.
publish.upload.archiveAlone: An archive sent first without a path is unpacked, so it must be the only file. Send a path field before each file to publish archives as files.
publish.upload.idle: The upload sent no data for {{seconds}} seconds, so Pinwall stopped waiting. Run the same command again before the upload URL expires.
publish.upload.interrupted: The upload was interrupted before all of it arrived. Run the same command again before the upload URL expires.

mcp.whoami.text: Signed in to {{url}} as {{name}} ({{role}}, via {{via}}). Isolation: {{isolation}}. Upload limit {{upload}} per publish; inline limit {{inline}}. Authoring notes:
mcp.notes.entry: The entry page is index.html or index.md at the top level of what you publish.
mcp.notes.relativeLinks: Use relative links and asset paths (css/site.css, not /css/site.css): every version is served under its own address.
mcp.notes.selfContained: Include every file the page needs; a version never changes after it is published.
mcp.notes.opaqueOrigin: Pages run in a sandbox without an origin of their own: cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and service workers do not work. Keep state in memory or in the URL.
mcp.notes.perVersionOrigin: Each version is served on its own origin: localStorage and cookies do not carry over between versions.

backup.busy: Another backup or restore is running (lease maintenance:backup). Try again when it has finished.
backup.leaseLost: The backup lease was lost, so stored files may have been removed meanwhile. Run the backup again.
backup.blobBad: Stored file {{sha}} is missing or does not match its SHA-256; the backup was not completed.
restore.notEmpty: The target is not empty ({{found}}). Restore into a new installation: an empty data directory, or an empty database and bucket prefix.
restore.notBackup: This is not a Pinwall backup archive.
restore.newerFormat: This backup was made by a newer Pinwall (backup format {{version}}). Upgrade Pinwall, then restore.
restore.unknownMigrations: This backup comes from a Pinwall with database migrations this version does not have ({{names}}). Upgrade Pinwall, then restore.
restore.damaged: The archive is damaged or incomplete: {{detail}}. Nothing was restored.
restore.changed: The target gained data while the restore was running. Nothing was restored.
restore.keyChanged: The secret key differs from the one that made this backup, so its identity-provider refresh tokens cannot be read. {{count}} single sign-on users must sign in again. To keep them signed in, restore with the original PINWALL_SECRET_KEY (on a SQLite install it is the secret.key file in the old data directory).
backup.outExists: {{path}} already exists. A backup never overwrites a file: choose another name, or remove it first.
backup.outTerminal: Standard output is a terminal, which would ruin the archive. Send it to a file or a pipe (with docker exec, leave out -t), or use --out <file>.
backup.schemaBehind: The database is at migration {{at}}, older than this Pinwall ({{version}}), which expects {{expected}}. A backup never migrates the database: back up with the Pinwall version that runs it, in the server's container or with the server's image.
backup.schemaAhead: The database is at migration {{at}}, which this Pinwall ({{version}}) does not know: it expects {{expected}}. A newer Pinwall runs this database: back up with that version, in the server's container or with the server's image.
spaces.guard.refused: PINWALL_VISIBILITY is team, but Pinwall last ran in personal mode and {{owners}} people own projects. In team mode every member would see all of their projects. To allow that, run pinwall visibility team --confirm once and start Pinwall again, or set PINWALL_VISIBILITY=personal.
spaces.guard.confirmed: Team mode confirmed: at the next start every member sees the projects of all {{owners}} owners.
